Mark Aesch, of Florida, to be Federal Transit Administrator, vice Marcus Molinaro.

Mikhail Bogachek, of Florida, to be Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the United States of America to the Republic of Kosovo.

Andreas Borgeas, of California, to be a Member of the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission of the United States for the term expiring September 30, 2028, vice Sylvia M. Becker, term expired.

John Burns, of South Carolina, to be Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the United States of America to the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

Pedro Cabrera, of Florida, to be Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the United States of America to the Republic of Guatemala.

WITHDRAWALS SENT TO THE SENATE:

 Lee Philip Rudofsky, of Arkansas, to be United States Circuit Judge for the Eighth Circuit, vice Bobby E. Shepherd, retiring, which was sent to the Senate on September 14, 2026.

item.description:

item.content:encoded:
A PROCLAMATION

For over 250 years, the liberties and freedoms of every American have been safeguarded by the heroic men and women who have faithfully served in the United States Armed Forces.  This Veterans Day, we honor our Nation’s cherished veterans and recommit to strengthen the support and resources they have so rightly earned.

From the battle for our independence during the Revolutionary War and the fight for the future of humanity in World War II to the ongoing battles to defend America’s security and protect her people, the countless veterans who have taken up arms have ensured that generations of Americans could enjoy the many blessings of our great Nation.  These selfless men and women have committed their lives to defending our families, our freedom, and our great American values.  We will never forget the price they have paid for our homeland.

As they sacrificed for our freedom, so too must our Nation ensure their welfare.  At my direction, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is restructuring to put veterans at the forefront of every decision.  The VA processed a record 3.1 million disability claims this year.  In my second term, we have also slashed the VA’s claims backlog by more than 70 percent and opened 47 new health care facilities, expanding access to world-class care for veterans in communities across our country.

Every American owes our veterans an eternal debt of gratitude, and no one who has worn our Nation’s uniform should ever be homeless.  That is why I will never stop fighting until every veteran has the housing and mental health support and treatment they need.  Additionally, I established the National Center for Warrior Independence last year with a goal of housing up to 6,000 homeless veterans by 2028.  Last year alone, we housed nearly 52,000 homeless veterans, the most in 7 years, and under my leadership, every veteran who served our Nation in the Armed Forces will have a place to call home.

item.content:encoded:
Section 1.  Purpose.  The American Dream of homeownership is a vital pillar of our great country.  It is the policy of my Administration to reduce regulatory barriers to mortgage origination and costs impeding homeownership; embrace innovative risk and value assessment technologies that incorporate Super Intelligence to drive down mortgage and homeownership costs; and promote competition and innovation throughout the housing and mortgage market.

Sec. 2.  Proactive Cancellation of Excessive Mortgage Insurance.  (a)  The Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency (Director) shall, if he determines that it is in the best interests of the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (Enterprises) or the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA), and the American public, direct the Enterprises to establish a pilot program, applicable only to mortgages made after the establishment of the pilot program, that periodically reviews single-family mortgage loans they own, guarantee, or securitize, using automated valuation models and other available data to assess current market value, and to identify borrowers who appear to satisfy equity and other requirements for cancellation of mortgage insurance.

(b)  The Director shall direct the Enterprises to establish procedures for the pilot program, including financial safety and soundness standards and payment-history requirements, under which mortgage insurance is canceled proactively when an Enterprise determines that:

(i)    the borrower satisfies applicable equity requirements based on the property’s current market value, as determined through an automated valuation model or other means approved by the Director;
